mainEntity.name: When is termite swarming season in New Jersey?

acceptedAnswer.text: In New Jersey, subterranean termite swarming typically occurs from late March through June, usually on warm, humid days immediately following a rainfall.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell a flying termite from a flying ant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flying termites have straight antennae, equal-sized wings, and a straight, broad waist. Winged ants have bent antennae, front wings larger than hind wings, and a pinched waist.

mainEntity.name: What does finding discarded wings in my house mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discarded wings near windows or doors are a strong indicator that a termite swarm has occurred inside or very close to your home, suggesting a mature colony is nearby.

mainEntity.name: Are swarming termites dangerous to touch?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, swarming termites do not bite or sting humans, and they do not consume structural wood themselves. Their sole purpose is to reproduce and start new colonies.

acceptedAnswer.text: Flooding oversaturates the soil and waterlogs structural wood, providing subterranean termites with the moisture and soft wood they need to survive and colonize.

mainEntity.name: How soon after a flood can termites attack a house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Termites can be attracted to wet wood within a few days to a few weeks post-flooding. Subterranean termites are highly moisture-dependent and migrate to wet foundation zones quickly.

mainEntity.name: Should I get a termite inspection after my basement floods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once the home is dried out, a professional termite inspection is highly recommended to ensure water-damaged sills and framing have not been compromised.

mainEntity.name: How do I dry out my crawl space to prevent termites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use high-capacity dehumidifiers, clean out wet insulation and debris, ensure crawl space vents are clear, and consult professionals for vapor barrier replacement.
